newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma rejects Russian government welfare cuts.
newsitem.headline: Duma rejects Russian government welfare cuts.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of parliament on Tuesday rejected five draft laws proposed by Russia's reformist government which aimed to cut welfare benefits but approved a sixth after ministers made serious concessions.

The government, trying to restore order to state finances, argues that the number of social benefits -- many of them a legacy of the heavily paternalistic Soviet system -- pose too great a burden for post-communist Russia's shaky economy.
The proposed cuts would mostly affect the poor and elderly, the main electorate of the communist-led opposition that dominates the Duma, which first rejected the package last week.
A conciliatory commission was formed to reconsider the measures after the first vote but the Duma threw out the revised drafts.

The Duma, which starts its summer recess on Wednesday, only backed a draft law on children's benefits after the government withdrew a proposal to cut the age of those entitled to the benefits to three years from 16 years.
On Monday the Duma also rejected government plans to slash spending under the 1997 budget by 108 trillion roubles ($18.8 billion) or about a fifth of the total.

The government has said that, with or without the support of the Duma, cuts in spending will take place because the state is simply unable to pay its bills. The cuts have been prompted by a big shortfall in tax revenue in the first three months of 1997.
